advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `facade_function` raise (as the deleted `_facade_function` did) instead of falling back to `getattr(rebar, name)` when no defining `_lib_*` module is found, so a stand-in is never silently measured.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_derive.py:282-286: `for module_name in _FACADE_MODULES: candidate = getattr(importlib.import_module(module_name), name, None) ... return getattr(rebar, name)`

Docstring at _mcp_derive.py:275-279 states the whole point is 'so a test that patches `rebar.<name>` before the server is built still derives the real signature' — the fallback defeats that guarantee for any symbol whose defining module is absent from `_FACADE_MODULES`
Deleted scripts/check_mcp_library_parity.py `_facade_function` raised: 'cannot resolve rebar\'s shipped `{symbol}`: ... refusing instead.' rather than returning the stand-in
advisory.finding: `facade_function` silently falls back to `getattr(rebar, name)` when no module in `_FACADE_MODULES` defines the symbol, so the MCP input signature can be derived from a test-patched stand-in rather than the shipped definition — the exact drift the deleted gate's `_facade_function` refused to measure. The deleted code raised a detailed RuntimeError ('The gate would otherwise measure that stand-in and report parity it never verified — refusing instead.'); the replacement makes that case invisible.
scenarios: A facade function is moved to a new `_lib_*` module not added to `_FACADE_MODULES`, while a test (or runtime) has rebound `rebar.<name>` to a stand-in before `build_server()`
Any symbol not defined by one of the six listed modules (the list omits `_lib_warn` and any future module)
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the final `return getattr(rebar, name)` with a RuntimeError naming the unresolved symbol and the module list, mirroring the deleted gate's refusal; or verify the resolved candidate's `__module__` is a rebar._lib_* module before returning.

evidence: Docstring at :277 claims resolution 'from its defining rebar._lib_* module rather than the rebar namespace'
_FACADE_MODULES is a fixed 6-tuple (:264-271); a facade function moved to or newly defined in any other module silently takes the fallback and derives from the facade namespace
ABSENCE: no error/warning distinguishes 'resolved from the defining module' from 'fell back to the facade namespace' — the two outcomes are indistinguishable at the call site
advisory.finding: facade_function() silently falls back to getattr(rebar, name) when the library function's defining module is not in the hardcoded _FACADE_MODULES tuple. The docstring promises it resolves the signature from the defining rebar._lib_* module 'so a test that patches rebar.<name> before the server is built still derives the real signature', but the fallback path derives from the (possibly patched or relocated) rebar namespace instead — contradicting the stated contract and deriving the wrong signature without any error.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the `return getattr(rebar, name)` fallback with a RuntimeError naming the symbol and _FACADE_MODULES, mirroring the deleted script's _facade_function which refused rather than measuring a stand-in.
